descriptionPlain:
Skyways designs, builds, and operates fully autonomous long range cargo aircraft. Founded in 2017, the company has spent nearly a decade developing and deploying autonomous logistics systems for real world operations.
Our V2 aircraft carries 30 lbs up to 500 miles, and V3 has a maximum range of well over 1,000 miles, a maximum useful load of 100 lbs, and a maximum endurance of nearly 20 hours. Both use a hybrid electric architecture that takes off like a helicopter and cruises like a plane, enabling long range autonomous delivery without traditional runway infrastructure.
Today, Skyways aircraft fly revenue missions for commercial customers across three continents. We are scaling full rate production and building toward large fleets of autonomous cargo aircraft.
Backed by Y Combinator and a $37M AFWERX STRATFI award from the U.S. Air Force, Skyways is creating a new form of transportation to advance our civilization from Austin, Texas.


The Opportunity
This role owns how autonomy works in real-world flight, and it owns the small team that builds it.

You will define how perception, state estimation, planning, and flight behaviors come together into a system that actually completes missions reliably. This is not about building isolated components. It is about making the full stack work under real constraints, and about leading a team of autonomy engineers to do the same.
You will shape how our ML systems improve with real-world data and ensure they perform outside of ideal conditions. You will lead technical direction for autonomy while remaining deeply hands-on in architecture, implementation, testing, and flight debugging. Your work directly impacts mission success, aircraft reliability, and operational deployment at fleet scale.
We are looking for someone who has already built and deployed autonomy systems on real-world robotic or UAV platforms, and who wants to grow a team while staying close to the code.

lists.content:
• Lead RCCA: Own every fleet reliability issue from intake through root cause, corrective action, validation, and permanent closure.

  • Follow the Scientific Method: Form hypotheses, design tests to prove or disprove them, and let evidence decide the root cause.

  • Solve the Hardest Problems Yourself: Troubleshoot failures across avionics, propulsion, power, EMI, software, and flight controls, and build the fix when that is the fastest path.

  • A strongly analytical mindset and a disciplined, evidence driven approach to root cause.

  • Experience leading RCCA or similar root cause and corrective action work on aircraft.

  • Hands on troubleshooting range across software, electrical, mechanical, and controls.

  • Deep command of methods like FMEA, fault tree analysis, 8D, and Weibull analysis.

  • Proficiency with Python or similar tools for data analysis.

  • Clear, direct communication with the whole organization: engineering, technicians, flight crews, and leadership.

• Experience with EMI and EMC investigation and mitigation.

• Build and assemble aircraft structures and systems from the ground up

• A&P license

  • UAS or military aircraft maintenance background

  • Flight line or flight test support experience
